title: Phase correction for ALMA. Investigating water vapour radiometer scaling: The long-baseline science verification data case study
question: Whether scaling the water vapour radiometer (WVR) solutions in wvrgcal improves phase correction, coherence and image S/N in ALMA long-baseline science verification data, and how the optimal scaling relates to weather conditions

data.bands: Bands 3, 4, 6, 7 (Juno B6; Mira B3, B6; HL Tau B3, B6, B7; SDP.81 B4, B6, B7)

recipe.method: Extract phases from widest single spectral window of bandpass calibrator and unwrap
Apply standard WVR solutions scaled by a range of factors to raw phases (via unity point-source dataset) and minimise the two-point-deviation of corrected phases
key_parameters: T = 6, 12, 32, 64 s; scale range 0.05-2.5, step 0.01; reference-antenna-only or all baselines

recipe.method: Coherence from exp(-phi_rms^2/2) using phase RMS over 60 s and full bandpass; ratio of scaled to standard WVR
Spearman rank correlation of scaling factors against weather parameters

recipe.goal: Image bandpass and science targets with and without scaling
recipe.method: Re-run reduction with scaling in wvrgcal; compare peak flux (dirty) and S/N (cleaned) of scaled vs standard
